description: Multi-tenancy for ASP.NET Core and EF Core: tenant resolution, access validation, and tenant isolation in a shared database or a database per tenant.
rules: Tenant-owned entities implement ITenantEntity<TKey> or derive from TenantEntity<TKey>; a TenantId property alone does nothing.
Entity types that implement neither are shared by every tenant by design; do not filter them by tenant yourself.
Register every DbContext that holds tenant-owned entities with options.UseTenantry().
Never set TenantId on new rows and never add Where(x => x.TenantId == ...) to queries: UseTenantry() stamps and filters.
Database.SqlQuery, SqlQueryRaw, ExecuteSql, ExecuteSqlRaw, ExecuteSqlInterpolated and IgnoreQueryFilters() are not tenant-isolated.
Pair ResolveFromHeader, ResolveFromRouteValue, ResolveFromQueryString, ResolveFromHost and ResolveFromSubdomain with ValidateTenantAccessByClaim or ValidateTenantAccess in the same AddTenantry.
Call app.UseTenantry() after app.UseAuthentication() and app.UseAuthorization(), before the endpoints.
Run background work from a tenant id with ITenantScopeFactory<TKey>.RunInScopeAsync(id, work), and await it; never block on it.
Pass CreateScope and MakeCurrent only a tenant read from the store, never a TenantDescriptor built from outside input.
Resolve a DbContext inside the tenant's scope; a database-per-tenant context throws if used after the current tenant changes.
Test isolation with Tenantry's real services and two tenants: one tenant must not read or write the other's rows.
